key_insight: Adding a KL-divergence regularizer to Wasserstein DRO prevents low-probability extreme events from being unrealistically overweighted, reducing over-conservative planning decisions.
engineering_relevance: The method gives power-system planners a more balanced way to size PV, wind, and storage under rare-but-severe renewable uncertainty.
method: Build a two-stage distributionally robust planning model for generation and storage investment.
Redefine the Wasserstein ambiguity set with a KL regularization term to curb probability inflation of extreme events.
Reformulate the model as an equivalent exponential cone program for tractable solution.
evidence_signal: Tests on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems show that standard Wasserstein DRO becomes over-conservative under low-probability extreme events, while the proposed model performs effectively and efficiently.
watch_item: The approach still depends on the assumed ambiguity-set parameters, so careful calibration is needed to avoid underestimating rare-event risk.
paper_title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
